chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ali al-Saqqaf, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was present, about a man who started with al-Marwah before al-Safa. He said: 'He must repeat [the sa'y]. Do you not see that if he started with his left hand before his right, he would be required to start with his right and then repeat on his left?'

And whoever performs extra sa'y beyond the seven circuits, if it was intentional, he is obliged to repeat the sa'y; and if it was by mistake, he discards what he added and counts himself as having completed the seven. Narrated.

key_terms.السَّعْيِ: Sa'y (the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.الْأَشْوَاطِ: Circuits (plural of shawt, referring to the seven trips)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim starts sa'y with Marwah before Safa or performs extra circuits?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the canonical order of Sa'y by starting at Safa, using the cultural norm of preferring the right hand to illustrate the importance of following the prescribed sequence. It further refines the jurisprudence of Hajj by distinguishing between intentional and unintentional deviations, showing how Shia fiqh accommodates human error while maintaining ritual integrity. This highlights the practical application of 'illah (effective cause) in deriving legal rulings from prophetic traditions.
